answer: When a hundred agents answer together, vote the same way, and attest only each other, the ledger treats them as one identity, not a hundred. A group-penalty rule clusters agents whose behaviour mirrors each other and splits one reward across the whole cluster, so a hundred clones earn no more than one honest agent. A healthy orchard has many different trees; a sybil farm is one tree copied a hundred times. Clones also strand themselves on an island, attesting only each other, so they hold no edges to the honest core. The attacker pays for a hundred identities and harvests one reward.
